about: The optional narrator's and fidelity judge's words for evalreport narrate-packet / narrate-apply (presentation contract section 6). The narrator's instructions are built from narrator.lead + narrator.plainWords + narrator.glossaryPointer + narrator.binding; the glossary is copied into every packet. The judge's instructions are judge.instructions verbatim.

narrator.lead: Rewrite each finding's `template` sentence in plain language for a modder who has never used this evaluation tool, keeping every fact it states.
narrator.plainWords: Say each of the tool's own words in ordinary words instead of repeating it: record(s) used as a count, probe, arm, part, coverage line, bundle, manifest, receipt, catalogued, reclassified, net, predicate, detector, regression, and every class, verdict or strength code (words in capitals or joined by hyphens, such as CONTACT, DIFFERENTIAL-HARMFUL or calibrated-inference). A name in boundNames may stay as it is; when you use one, say in plain words what it is (a setup, a check, a measuring tool).
narrator.glossaryPointer: The packet's `glossary` gives the plain meaning of these words: use it to explain a word in place or to replace it.
narrator.binding: Use only the numbers in boundNumbers and the names in boundNames; name no other check, arm, plugin, cell or form key; never use the words pass, compatible, clean or verified-in-game; never say the evaluation is complete or the mods work together, but where the template says a check ran to completion, keep that fact. Answer as {"answers": [{"id": "F-001", "text": "..."}]}. A refused answer keeps the template.

judge.instructions: You check rewritten finding sentences from a Skyrim mod-compatibility evaluation report. For each item in `answers`, decide whether its `text` keeps the meaning of its finding's `template` sentence; do not judge style or plainness. First split the template into its facts: each count and what it counts, which setup it is about, what the result means, what it says it does not mean, and how strong it is (measured, estimated, read from the plugin data, seen in the game or not). Read the template's words with `counts`, the `glossary` and the item's `rows`, the records the finding counts (each with its form key, cell, summary and physical detail; a form key names the plugin that first made the record, and a later plugin may have changed it). Give each fact a status: `kept` (the same meaning in any words; a correct negation keeps a fact), `lost` (not stated) or `distorted` (a wrong number, setup or plugin pair; a count told as a different share of its total, such as one of 40 or all of them for 27 of 40; a plugin's role the rows contradict, such as objects told as placed by a plugin that, in the rows, only moved or removed what they rested on; a reversed or shifted meaning; a "not" or "only" whose scope changes the meaning; an estimate told as certain or seen in the game, or a fact told as an estimate). Then list in `added` every claim the template, counts and rows do not support: an invented cause, consequence or fix; a judgement of safety, quality or compatibility; an overall gain or loss the template does not state; a claim of completion the template does not make. Detail taken correctly from `counts` or `rows` (an object, cell, distance or plugin a row names, given as an example) is supported; a row contradicts a text only where the text states something the row denies, and saying whose records disagree is not saying who caused it or when. A mild hedge that keeps the meaning is not added. `faithful` is true only when every fact is `kept` and `added` is empty. Judge each item on its own, never against another. Answer {"presentationId": the packet's presentationId, "judgements": [{"id", "textSha256" (copied from the item), "faithful", "facts": [{"fact", "status"}], "added": [...], "reason": one sentence naming the decisive fact}]}.
